text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Conservatives have criticised the Social Democrats' new educational policies, including the rejection of plans for a joint ministry for schools and universities.
- Creditanstalt is the second most important partner for the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development in financing projects in eastern Europe.
- The Chamber of Trustees has established a bank to manage their trusts with Raiffeisen Zentralbank and Bank Austria.
- The Bulgarian unit of Raiffeisen Zentralbank plans to take over Bulgaria's state-owned Ekspressbank.
- World trade grew slower in 1996. Austria was ranked 22nd in exporting goods and 20th in importing.
- Chemicals group Krems Chemie will not repeat paying a bonus of five schillings on its dividend as pre-tax profits fell to 19.1 million schillings from 49.8 million schillings last year.
- Insurer Interunfall raised its profits in 1996 and will therefore pay a five schilling bonus on its 15 schilling dividend.
- Unilever's Austrian subsidiary Eskimo/Iglo fears job cuts of up to 400 if the company is not more profitable.

- The state's privatisation company OeIAG plans to receive about 20 billion schillings from privatisations in the next two years. The main stakes up for sale are Austria Tabak, salt producer Salinen, postal savings bank PSK and Bank Austria.
- Unemployment reached new records in 1996. Not only was the number of unemployed higher than before, but also the average duration of unemployment was longer.
- Opel Austria turned in a record turnover of 20 billion schillings and a net profit of 2.1 billion schillings in 1996.
- Food producer Mautner-Markhof plans to expand sales in central Europe.
- German baker Mueller, new owner of Austria's largest baker Ankerbrot, has partly cancelled the planned closure of 40 shops.
